title: Overview
text: wrf_gpu User's Guide A GPU-native, WRF-compatible regional weather model · v0.23.2 wrf_gpu runs a standalone WRF v4 ARW forecast end-to-end on a single GPU. It reads a standard WRF namelist.input, initializes from WRF real-data artifacts (wrfinput_* and wrfbdy_d01; no CPU-WRF wrfout dependency), integrates a nonhydrostatic split-explicit ARW dynamical core on the GPU, and writes a WRF-compatible wrfout history file. Built on the shoulders of WRF. This project is an independent, AI-written re-implementation of the same physics solver, GPU-optimized and validated cell-for-cell against WRF as the result oracle. It is not a port of the WRF Fortran source and is not affiliated with or endorsed by UCAR/NCAR. The Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model is developed and maintained by NCAR/UCAR and the WRF community; please cite and credit them. See Credits, License & Citation. title: How wrf_gpu Works
text: How wrf_gpu Works wrf_gpu is a clean-room JAX rewrite of the WRF-ARW forecast model that targets the GPU memory hierarchy from day one. It reproduces the same physics solver WRF implements, but its architecture, execution model, and validation strategy are built for the GPU — not inherited from the WRF Fortran source. wrf_gpu is not a line-by-line translation of WRF Fortran and it is not a CUDA-annotated copy of the WRF codebase. It is an independent implementation of the WRF-ARW equations and physics, written in JAX and compiled to the GPU through XLA. It reads the same inputs as WRF and writes WRF-compatible output, but the solver in between is its own code, held to WRF's numerical behavior by validation rather than by shared source. Why this matters for you Because it is a rewrite validated against an oracle, wrf_gpu can be honest and precise about exactly which parts match WRF and how well. The dynamics/thermodynamics core is proven cell-for-cell identical to CPU-WRF v4; the broader forecast-skill equivalence over 24–72 h is a separate, still-open gate. The guide never blurs those two. title: GPU-native architecture
text: The design follows a small set of immutable principles: Whole-state device residency. After initialization the full model state lives on the GPU. There are no host↔device transfers inside the timestep loop (any exception requires an architecture decision record). Fused, timestep-scale kernels. The integrator compiles into a few large fused programs rather than a storm of tiny kernel launches, so the GPU stays busy instead of waiting on launch overhead. fp64 dynamical core. title: Validation against WRF, not bitwise reproducibility
text: wrf_gpu does not aim to be bit-for-bit identical to a specific WRF build (which is impossible across compilers and core counts anyway). Instead it validates against WRF as an oracle through a tiered pyramid, strongest evidence first: Micro-fixture / savepoint parity — individual physics kernels checked against pristine-WRF single-column oracles to machine precision. Physical invariants — conservation and boundedness checks. Short-run / convergence — behavior over the first forecast hours. title: The priority order
text: When two goals conflict, wrf_gpu resolves them in a fixed order: stability > identity > speed > memory A result is never destabilized or altered to go faster or fit in less memory. This is why the default path stays fp64 and byte-identical across releases, and why performance features (batched ensembles, fp32, fused warm-start) are opt-in or value-preserving — they never move the default numbers. See Performance & GPU Modes.

title: Quickstart: Your First Forecast
text: Quickstart: Your First Forecast Run the bundled Switzerland 3 km case — real GFS-initialized inputs that ship in the repo — end-to-end on your GPU in three commands, then read the WRF-compatible wrfout it writes. No external data download, no local real.exe step, no CPU-WRF run required. Before you start You need wrf_gpu installed with a GPU-visible JAX (Installation & Requirements). The bundled case selects RRTMG radiation and Noah-MP land; Noah-MP reads WRF lookup tables, so set GPUWRF_WRF_ROOT to a pristine WRF v4 tree first. This case needs only GPUWRF_WRF_ROOT — GPUWRF_CANAIRY_ROOT is for the larger validation corpus, not this case. # 1. Point at a pristine WRF v4 source/run tree (for the RRTMG + Noah-MP tables): export GPUWRF_WRF_ROOT=/path/to/WRF # 2. Run one forecast hour of the bundled Switzerland 3 km case on the GPU: python -m gpuwrf.cli run \ --input-dir examples/switzerland_d01 \ --output-dir runs/switzerland_d01 \ --domain d01 \ --hours 1 \ --scratch-dir /fast/nvme/scratch # any real (non-tmpfs) fast disk # 3. Read the WRF-compatible history file: ncdump -h runs/switzerland_d01/wrfout_d01_* Raise --hours for a longer forecast — the bundled namelist window covers 24 h.

title: Single-domain vs. nested
text: Nesting is explicit opt-in via --max-dom N. A multi-domain namelist (max_dom > 1) does not silently become a nested run: without --max-dom, run executes a single domain (--domain) and prints a note reminding you to pass --max-dom N for the live-nested forecast. With --max-dom > 1, the standalone live-nested driver runs d01..dN together, the parent building each child's lateral boundary live (no pre-supplied wrfbdy_d02). Mechanics: Nesting.

title: Restart
text: wrf_gpu supports the standard WRF restart mechanism as part of its initialization path — restart is bit-identity-validated, and the per-domain subcycling nested path supports it as well. Restart cadence is governed by the usual namelist.input keys (restart, restart_interval); the restart file carries the WRF-faithful state (for example the 1 km inner-nest qke cold-start seed) so a restarted run picks up where it left off.

title: Two-way nesting (--feedback)
text: Opt-in For nested runs, --feedback enables two-way nesting: after each child finishes its subcycle, its interior is fed back onto the overlapping parent cells (WRF copy_fcn area-average plus the sm121 feedback-zone smoother). The default is one-way nesting — the validated wiring. Two-way feedback is finite and stable but its 24 h skill equivalence is untested, so it is off by default.

title: Station scoring (--score)
text: --score additionally scores the forecast against AEMET station observations. It requires GPUWRF_AEMET_ROOT and is not part of the README runnability gate — leave it off for a plain forecast.

title: VRAM preflight & --force-gpu-run
text: For nested runs (--max-dom > 1) the CLI runs a fast, CPU-side VRAM-headroom preflight before the (multi-minute) compile and fails closed with exit 75 instead of OOMing tens of minutes in. title: Input Data & Initialization
text: Input Data & Initialization wrf_gpu keeps the WRF run artifacts you already know: namelist.input, wrfinput_*, and wrfbdy_d01. It integrates those real-data inputs on the GPU with no CPU-WRF wrfout dependency, and auto-detects a legacy replay path when CPU-WRF wrfout history is present. Usage parity with WRF If you already run WRF, the biggest change is that wrf_gpu replaces wrf.exe with a single command, python -m gpuwrf.cli run. You keep your WRF real-data case directory and namelist.input; the supported namelist matrix runs as-is, and anything unsupported fails closed with a named reason. Operational The primary path is standalone native-init. The current CLI reads the model's initial state from wrfinput_<domain> and the root lateral-boundary forcing from wrfbdy_d01. There is no CPU-WRF wrfout replay in the loop; the forecast state is advanced by wrf_gpu on the GPU. A standalone case directory looks like a normal WRF real-data case: my_case/ ├── namelist.input # standard WRF v4 ARW namelist (bring your own) ├── wrfinput_d01 # initial state (one per domain you run) ├── wrfinput_d02 ├── wrfbdy_d01 # lateral boundaries for the outer domain └── met_em.d0*.*.nc # met_em-stage forcing

title: Dynamical Core
text: Dynamical Core wrf_gpu integrates a nonhydrostatic, split-explicit ARW dynamical core on the GPU — the same architecture as WRF's Advanced Research WRF core, re-implemented in JAX and validated cell-for-cell against CPU-WRF as the oracle. The dynamics/thermodynamics core is proven cell-for-cell identical to CPU-WRF v4; the priority order in every design decision is stability > identity > speed > memory, with no masking, clamping, or nan_to_num on the result path. The core uses WRF's split-explicit time scheme. A third-order Runge-Kutta (RK3) large step advances the slow (meteorologically significant) modes, while the fast acoustic and gravity-wave modes are integrated with smaller acoustic sub-steps inside each RK3 stage. Only rk_order=3 is supported. Prognostic variables are advanced with flux-form advection. The advection orders are frozen to the WRF real-data default (5th-order horizontal, 3rd-order vertical). title: Nesting
text: Nesting wrf_gpu runs one-way live nesting — d01 → d02 → d03, down to a 1 km inner nest — entirely on the GPU. The parent domain advances and builds each child's lateral boundary live during the run, so you do not need a pre-supplied wrfbdy_d02. The child's initial condition comes from its own wrfinput_d0N; only wrfbdy_d01 forces the root. There is no CPU-WRF wrfout dependency. The nested driver is a standalone recursion faithful to WRF's module_integrate sub-cycling: the parent advances one step, constructs each child's lateral-boundary package from its own freshly-advanced state, and recurses into the child, which sub-cycles to catch up to the parent's clock. Each child's boundary update cadence is its parent's timestep. This is the validated one-way wiring (parent → child; the child does not modify the parent). The nest refinement is set by the WRF &domains key parent_grid_ratio (the spatial refinement, e.g. 3), read from the domain metadata. text: The nest refinement is set by the WRF &domains key parent_grid_ratio (the spatial refinement, e.g. 3), read from the domain metadata. text: Nested runs support the wrfrst-equivalent restart: the full per-domain physics carry is snapshotted and reloads bit-for-bit to continue the forecast. See Output Files.

title: Opt-in two-way feedback
text: Two-way nesting is opt-in via the --feedback flag (nested runs only). title: Validation & WRF Identity
text: Validation & WRF Identity wrf_gpu is validated by a reproducible, CPU-only identity-proof system that compares a GPU wrfout against a CPU-WRF wrfout from the same initialization, over all grid cells, all forecast leads, and all core prognostic variables, against a frozen tolerance manifest that is read before comparison and never tuned. WRF is the oracle; this is the project's primary fidelity gate. Cell-identity is a per-cell, per-lead, per-variable proof — not an aggregate station-RMSE summary. title: The extreme-terrain ceiling (~6000 m)
text: The Alpine / Mont-Blanc extreme-terrain boundary instability is fixed (WRF-faithful zero-gradient physical W + specified-boundary cadence, no masking). The remaining ceiling is ~6000 m: a nest over ~8000 m terrain (Karakoram) still diverges to a non-finite state — which the default-on finite guard catches and fails closed (0 bad frames written), and on which WRF's own real.exe likewise fails without a lowered etac. The deep > 6000 m fix is a future dycore-boundary milestone; the validated production envelope is steep real-world terrain up to ~6000 m.

title: Free-running open-boundary stability
text: Free-running without lateral-boundary relaxation on wide domains (nx ≈ 160+) can go unstable beyond ~14 h. The validated operational path uses boundary forcing (KI-7). See Dynamical Core → Boundaries.

title: Out-of-memory behavior
text: The co-resident-headroom OOM mode is solved by the launch-time VRAM preflight (fail-closed exit 75). The solo cuda_async fragmentation mode is mitigated, not fixed: a bit-identical RRTMG column-tile cap cuts the radiation transient's largest allocation −37 %, but solo fragmentation can still OOM the full fp64 nest, and the long-horizon 9-nest can OOM around the ~90 min integration horizon (a reproducer ships). The default-on finite guard aborts cleanly with {domain, field, level, step, sim-time, index} rather than propagating a corrupted state. No OOM-proof guarantee is made.
